evals.name: clinical-registry-regulated
evals.prompt: We're starting a new project from scratch. Attached is the requirement doc my consultant wrote for a surgical outcomes database — patient details, surgeon operation data, post-op histology, and follow-up questionnaires the patient fills in. Can you turn this into a proper spec so we can start building?
evals.expected_output: intent.md and spec.md. Onion table fully filled with no blank cells. Must surface: an administrative/maintenance role, the regulator, a negative stakeholder, and interfacing systems — none of which appear in the source doc. Must flag fields that are both entered and derived. Must use NEEDS CLARIFICATION rather than inventing thresholds.

evals.name: internal-tool-spreadsheet-replacement
evals.prompt: ok so right now our ops team tracks every client onboarding in a shared google sheet and it's a disaster, people overwrite each other constantly. i want to build a proper little internal web app for it. columns are: client name, account manager, contract signed date, kickoff call date, docs received y/n, status (not started / in progress / blocked / done), and notes. write me the spec for it
evals.expected_output: intent.md and spec.md. Should identify the current spreadsheet owner as a negative stakeholder, migration as in scope, an admin/maintenance role, and who maintains the tool afterwards. Should question status lifecycle and permissions. Should not over-engineer a small internal tool.

evals.name: external-actor-consumer-facing
evals.prompt: I need a spec for a customer returns portal. Customer enters their order number and email, picks the items to return and a reason, gets a printable label, and we track the return until refund. Should integrate with our existing order system. Can you write this up properly before we hand it to the dev team?
evals.expected_output: intent.md and spec.md. Should surface: identity/auth story for a non-staff actor, operational support path when the order number doesn't match, the ops staff who process returns, the admin who configures return reasons and windows, fraud as a negative stakeholder, and the order system as an interfacing system.
